- Acute diarrhoea for ~3 days with abdominal pain and one episode of vomiting; patient remains hydrated with no red flags noted; management focused on dietary modification, hydration, and close follow-up.

  - Three days of diarrhoea with abdominal pain; four to five bowel movements per day.
  - Stool description: mixture of watery and loose consistency; no blood or mucus reported.
  - One episode of vomiting early in the course.
  - Appetite reduced but patient remains able to drink fluids.
  - No recent travel or questionable food intake; no known outside dietary exposure.
  - No medications started for diarrhoea or abdominal pain yet.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute diarrhoea (no dehydration or red flags observed at presentation)
  - Plan:
    - Diet: Implement a soft diet during diarrhoea (avoid dairy, fish, meat, eggs initially).
      - Soft diet examples: crackers, toast, jam; easily digested foods.
      - Gradual reintroduction: after ~48 hours with holding diarrhoea, introduce boiled vegetables and mash; if tolerating, progress to meats; avoid heavy/meat-containing foods while diarrhoea persists to prevent relapse.
    - Hydration: Emphasize adequate fluid intake; consider Dioralyte rehydration solution OTC to replenish electrolytes.
    - Probiotics: Yogurt recommended to aid gut flora recovery.
    - Timing for advancing diet: If diarrhoea improves for ~48 hours with no new symptoms, proceed with gradual reintroduction; avoid large meat intake until gut recovers.
    - Warning signs / when to seek care:
      - If diarrhoea persists > 1 week.
      - If diarrhoea increases to 6–8+ stools per day or signs of dehydration develop (hospitalization may be required).
      - If blood in stool.
    - Follow-up / monitoring:
      - Return if symptoms worsen or do not resolve in a week.
      - Education provided and notes accessible in the app for reference.
      - Reassurance about not needing immediate antibiotics unless stool culture indicates infection.
  - Rationale: Diarrhoea description and clinical course consistent with self-limited gastroenteritis; stool blood/mucus absent; dehydration not evident on clinical impression.

- Issue 2: Asthma and current medications
  - Plan:
    - Clarify inhaler use and current asthma management at follow-up (transcript shows ambiguity around inhaler and Lexapro; dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - No acute asthma treatment initiated today.
  - Rationale: Transcript contains conflicting information about asthma medications (Lexapro vs inhaler); documentation incomplete.

- General notes:
  - Education provided regarding dietary management, hydration, and warning signs.
  - Documentation of plan and notes available in patient app.
